_comment: Canonical figures. If a number in here appears on a page, it must appear
with THIS value — scripts/claims-guard.mjs fails the build otherwise.
This exists because two blog posts drifted from $9 to $12 for Make Core
and nobody noticed for months, and because the guard meant to catch that
had the kit price hardcoded in its own allowlist, so moving the kit off
$29 broke the build instead of being caught by it.
Prices under `ours` are ours to set: no vendor source needed, and they
mirror src/data/products.ts, which stays the source of truth for anything
rendered. Everything under `thirdParty` is somebody else's number and
carries the date a human last read it on the vendor's own pricing page.
Do not edit a verifiedDate without opening that page.

_scope: RECURRING. This was recorded as "USD one-time" until 4 Sep 2026,
which contradicted the UnitPriceSpecification of MONTH that /about/
had been emitting beside it. $7.99 once and $7.99 a month are not the
same offer and the unit is the whole difference.
The contexts below deliberately match nothing in src/pages/about.astro
or src/components/StockLogPromo.astro: both now render the constant,
so there is no literal left in them to drift. What the patterns do
guard is public/llms.txt and public/llms-full.txt, which are static
text a crawler and a model read and which cannot import anything.
Those two are the only places the number is still written by hand.
Note how claims-guard treats contexts: a match is reported only when
the stated value appears in `retired`. With `retired` empty these
patterns are armed and loaded with nothing, which is correct today —
7.99 has had no predecessor. The moment the price moves, adding the
old figure to `retired` turns them live against every file above.

metaEmqScore.value: unmeasured — no EMQ figure is published
_scope: EMQ is not a price, so neither guard looked at it. public/llms.txt carried
"typical EMQ 7–8.5" until 21 Sep 2026 — three weeks after /capi-shield/ had
already retracted it in prose — and llms.txt is the file AI assistants quote
verbatim. The same figure survived in llms-full.txt, ai-plugin.json, a diagram
<desc>, the TikTok page's stat strip ("6–8 EMQ score typical", contradicting
that page's own FAQ) and a fabricated per-event benchmark table on the EMQ
estimator ("Purchase 8.8–9.3").
`retired` and `contexts` stay empty on purpose: there is no correct number to
drift from. The whole claim is retired, so the work is done by `forbid`.
What is still allowed, and deliberately not matched below: describing the 0–10
scale, naming the match keys the score is calculated from, and telling a reader
to read their own score. What is forbidden is any number presented as a score
scale, naming the match keys the score is calculated from, and telling a reader
to read their own score. What is forbidden is any number presented as a score
this site's setups produce, as a benchmark to hit, or as a per-key point lift.
Ranges are matched through HTML entities as well as literal dashes. The first
cut of these patterns only knew [-–—], so it passed the whole EMQ section of
/blog/shopify-server-side-tracking-complete-setup-guide/, where every range is
written 4–5. An .astro file is the place a claim is most likely to be
entity-encoded, so a pattern that cannot read an entity is not a guard.

attributionLossFigure.value: unmeasured — no loss or recovery percentage is published
attributionLossFigure.unit: share of purchase-conversion signal lost to ATT/ITP/ad blockers, or recovered by server-side
_scope: The 20–40% figure was retracted on 4 Sep 2026 — withdrawn, not revised. Two
weeks later it was still being published as 35% in /capi-shield/'s hero, 40%
on /tools/, 15–35% on /make-com-shopify/ and eleven separate figures in
/blog/shopify-server-side-tracking-complete-setup-guide/. A retraction that
lives in one page's prose is a note, not a retraction.
The patterns are deliberately plain: a loss/recovery verb, a percentage and a
noun the figure is denominated in, in any of the three orders English puts
them. Everything subtle lives in `unless`, which is checked against the line
the match sits on. The first draft encoded the exemptions as tempered tokens
inside the patterns and became unreadable; a named list is reviewable.
The filler token matches a whole HTML tag as well as plain text: the hero on
/capi-shield/ read "losing 35% of its conversion data", and a
filler of [^<] walked straight past it. Same lesson as the EMQ entry's entity
dashes — a claim in an .astro file is rarely plain prose.
WHAT `unless` LETS THROUGH, and why each one has to be allowed:
1. retract/withdraw/no longer/publishes no — the site has to name the
figure in order to retract it. /about/, /how-we-test/, the benchmark
page and src/data/attributionGap.js `retractions[]` all do. A guard
that fires on the retraction notice pushes you to delete the record.
2. documented…case / denominated in it — the benchmark's one sourced row,
the ~40% attributable-conversion loss without CAPI. n=1, cited, dated,
and deliberately still published; how-we-test says exactly what it is
worth. THIS IS THE SOFT SPOT: the words 'documented case' beside a
number are enough to pass. The guard stops a retracted figure creeping
back. It cannot certify a new one — that still needs a human to open
the citation.
3. abandoned cart / checkout — cart-recovery rates are a different
quantity with real industry sourcing, not tracking signal loss.
4. cumulative miss rate / silently drops — the 99.5%-of-orders reliability
arithmetic in the automations guide, which is about scenario failure.
5. the CSS tokens — `.pro-block { background: linear-gradient(…0%…)` is a
class name and a gradient stop, not a claim.
NOT exempted, and not needing to be: bands for reading a reader's OWN
measurement ('a gap above 35% indicates a problem', 'under 20% is normal')
carry no loss verb next to the figure. App-COST recovery (the 50/85/100%
levels on the cost calculator) and affiliate commission rates are money, not
signal, so the noun list excludes them by construction.
Every VERB alternative is anchored with \b. Without it `miss` matched inside
`commission` and the guard failed the build on an affiliate commission rate.
The rest of `unless` is mechanical rather than editorial: CSS declarations
(`display: block`, `width: 100%`), the cost calculator's <option> labels, a
scroll-depth note, the gap calculator's innerHTML template — which prints the
READER's own computed gap and must keep doing so — and the cart post's
'total recoveries' line. None of them is a published loss figure.

_comment: Press mentions. A press credential is a set of facts about somebody else's
publication, and it drifts exactly the way the Make Core price drifted:
right on one page, a month out on another. src/data/press.ts is what
renders; this block is the independent copy that catches an edit to one
and not the other. Change both together, or the build fails.
`forbidNear` catches a wrong date stated beside the outlet name.
`url` also scopes the rating-markup check: a Review, Rating,
AggregateRating, EndorsementRating or Award node near this URL fails the
build. A contributed quote is an Article the person is a subject of.
Marking it as a rating of us is structured-data spam and risks a manual
action — see CLAUDE.md.
